title: Cupertino Lights First Lamp as Bay Area Diwali Season Opens at Memorial Park
excerpt: The Cupertino Chamber of Commerce's free festival at Memorial Park on October 17 drew families, business leaders, Consul General Satish Sivan and Mayor Kitty Moore for the inaugural lamp-lighting.
body:
• Cupertino's Bay Area Diwali Festival of Lights was held on Saturday, October 17, from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. at Memorial Park, 21121 Stevens Creek Blvd., with free admission.
  • The Cupertino Chamber of Commerce organized the festival; India Abroad reported Consul General Satish Sivan as chief guest at the inaugural lamp-lighting ceremony, joined by Cupertino Mayor Kitty Moore.
  • The program featured Indian food, cultural performances and a rangoli display, plus arts and crafts booths and a dedicated kids zone.
  • Bay Area families can still plan ahead: Diwali itself falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, and the Cupertino festival is a free way to start the season without tickets.

Diwali celebrations began in Cupertino on Saturday, October 17, as residents and business leaders gathered at Memorial Park for the Bay Area Diwali Festival of Lights, according to New India Abroad. The event ran from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. and was organized by the Cupertino Chamber of Commerce, which has hosted the festival at the park for more than two decades.

India Abroad reported that Consul General Satish Sivan attended as chief guest at the inaugural lamp-lighting ceremony, joined by Cupertino Mayor Kitty Moore. The lighting marked the formal start of a day built around Diwali's message of hope, friendship and harmony, and around the cultural ties between India and the Bay Area.

A Full Day at Memorial Park

The festival program combined food, performance and hands-on activities. Family listings for the event described a feast of food, cultural performances and a traditional rangoli display, along with arts and crafts booths and a kids zone. The organizer's festival description adds the range of dance forms that have become a fixture of the day, from classical Kathak and Bharatanatyam to Bhangra and Bollywood numbers, alongside a Kids Zone packed with activities for younger children.

The scale is well established. In its recap of a recent edition, the City of Cupertino noted that thousands of attendees came to Memorial Park for multicultural performances, music and dance, with more than 70 vendors offering crafts, jewelry and food. Admission and parking have traditionally been free, which has helped the event draw families from across Silicon Valley rather than only from Cupertino itself.

Why Cupertino Matters for Diwali in America

Cupertino sits at the center of one of the largest Indian-American communities in the United States, and its Diwali festival has grown into a civic event rather than a purely community one. The presence of both the Indian consul general and the city's mayor at the lamp-lighting reflects that shift: Diwali is now part of the public calendar in the Bay Area, not only a celebration inside homes and temples.

The timing adds to that visibility. Diwali itself falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, with the five-day festival running from November 6 to November 10, according to Bay Area festival guides. California added Diwali to its list of official state holidays in 2025, a change those guides say has amplified the festival's cultural significance for schools, employers and public agencies across the state.

What It Means for Bay Area Families

For Indian-American families in Cupertino, Sunnyvale, Fremont and San Jose, the Memorial Park festival is usually the first large public stop of the season, weeks before Lakshmi Puja at home. It offers children a public version of traditions they otherwise see mainly within the family: diyas, rangoli, classical dance and festival food in one place, presented in a way that classmates and neighbors of every background can share.

Readers who missed the Cupertino event still have options across the region through early November, including temple celebrations and community melas listed in Bay Area Diwali guides. Organizers of the Cupertino festival encourage attendees to RSVP in advance for future editions, even though entry is free, so the Chamber can plan food, parking and the kids zone for the crowds the event reliably draws.
